Beck has contributed three new songs—"Cities", "Touch the People" and "Spiral Staircase"—to the video game ''[[Sound Shapes]]'' for [[PlayStation 3]], [[PlayStation 4]], and [[PlayStation Vita]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stereogum.com/1125002/beck-cities-spiral-staircase-touch-the-people/mp3s|title=Beck – "Cities," "Spiral Staircase," & "Touch The People" – Stereogum|work=Stereogum|date=August 14, 2012|access-date=April 21, 2020|archive-date=July 28, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200728235258/https://www.stereogum.com/1125002/beck-cities-spiral-staircase-touch-the-people/mp3s/|url-status=live}}</ref> Beck collaborated on two songs for [[Childish Gambino]]'s "Royalty" mixtape in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.com/2012/05/even-beck-cant-save-childish-gambinos-messy-silk-pillow/|title=Even Beck Can't Save Childish Gambino's Messy 'Silk Pillow'|work=SPIN|date=May 31, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2018|archive-date=April 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180405154527/https://www.spin.com/2012/05/even-beck-cant-save-childish-gambinos-messy-silk-pillow/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2014, Beck collaborated with [[Sia]] for the song "Moonquake Lake", which is featured in the [[Annie (2014 film soundtrack)|soundtrack]] for the 2014 [[Annie (2014 film)|''Annie'']] film.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rigby|first1=Sam|title=Sia and Beck Join Stars on Annie Movie Soundtrack|url=http://www.digitalspy.com/music/news/a605383/sia-and-beck-join-stars-on-annie-movie-soundtrack.html|website=digitalspy.com|date=October 23, 2014|publisher=Digital Spy|access-date=November 3, 2014|archive-date=November 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104005343/http://www.digitalspy.com/music/news/a605383/sia-and-beck-join-stars-on-annie-movie-soundtrack.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2015, Beck collaborated with former [[Fun (band)|Fun.]] frontman [[Nate Ruess]] on the single "What This World Is Coming To", which was one of the Grammy-winning artist's many works featured on his debut solo album ''[[Grand Romantic]]'' released in June 2015. He also collaborated with [[electronic dance music]] duo [[The Chemical Brothers]] on their album ''[[Born in the Echoes]]'', providing lead vocals and also credited in writing for the track "Wide Open", released in July.<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Kreps|first1=Daniel|title=Chemical Brothers Continue Robot Fascination With Beck Collabo Video|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/chemical-brothers-continue-robot-fascination-with-beck-collabo-video-20160125|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|access-date=October 25, 2017|date=January 25, 2016|archive-date=October 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171026110655/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/chemical-brothers-continue-robot-fascination-with-beck-collabo-video-20160125|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2016, Beck collaborated with French [[electronic music]] band [[M83 (band)|M83]], providing vocals for the song "Time Wind" from their album ''[[Junk (M83 album)|Junk]]''. He was also featured on "Tiny Cities" by [[Flume (musician)|Flume]]. He also collaborated with [[Lady Gaga]] on the song "Dancin' in Circles", from her 2016 album ''[[Joanne (Lady Gaga album)|Joanne]]''.<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Browne|first1=David|title=Lady Gaga's 'Joanne': Mark Ronson on Producing 'Raw and Exposed' New Album|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/mark-ronson-on-lady-gagas-raw-and-exposed-joanne-w445356|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|access-date=October 25, 2017|date=October 18, 2016|archive-date=October 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019192054/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/mark-ronson-on-lady-gagas-raw-and-exposed-joanne-w445356|url-status=live}}</ref>

Also in 2016, during a pre-show for the [[58th Annual Grammy Awards|Grammy Awards]], Beck collaborated with the surviving members of the band [[Nirvana (band)|Nirvana]] to play Nirvana's rendition of [[The Man Who Sold the World (song)|"The Man Who Sold the World"]] as a tribute to both [[David Bowie]], who had died just 1 month earlier, and [[Kurt Cobain]], the former lead singer of Nirvana.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Surviving members of Nirvana team up with Beck to cover David Bowie's 'Man Who Sold The World' |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/news/nirvana-beck-cover-david-bowie-man-who-sold-the-world-mtv-unplugged-dave-grohl-kurt-cobain-a6876526.html |last=Shepherd |first=Jack |access-date=April 29, 2023 |date=February 16, 2016 |work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> Beck and Nirvana teamed up once again in 2020 for a fundraiser event, alongside [[St. Vincent (musician)|St. Vincent]] and [[Dave Grohl]]'s Daughter Violet Grohl.<ref>{{Cite magazine |title=Dave Grohl Reunites With Nirvana Members For Special Performance|access-date=April 29, 2023 |date=January 5, 2020 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/nirvana-reunion-2020-dave-grohl-krist-novoselic-pat-smear-beck-st-vincent-933688/ |last=Chan |first=Tim}}</ref>

In 2017, Beck appeared in the multiple award-winning film ''[[The American Epic Sessions]]'', directed by [[Bernard MacMahon (filmmaker)|Bernard MacMahon]]. He recorded "14 Rivers, 14 Floods" backed by a full gospel choir, live onto the first [[History of sound recording#The electrical era (1925 to 1945) (including sound on film)|electrical sound recording]] system from the 1920s.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wired.com/2017/05/american-epic-return-of-the-lathe/|title=The Long-Lost, Rebuilt Recording Equipment That First Captured the Sound of America|magazine=WIRED|access-date=February 4, 2018|language=en-US|archive-date=December 30, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171230172640/https://www.wired.com/2017/05/american-epic-return-of-the-lathe/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2021, Beck collaborated with [[Paul McCartney]] to make his hit single "Find My Way" on the album ''[[McCartney III Imagined]]''.

In 2023, Beck collaborated with The Chemical Brothers for the second time on the song "Skipping like a Stone". This was the fourth single to be released from their album ''[[For That Beautiful Feeling]]''.

In 2024, Beck appeared on the song, "Boom Boom Back" by the band, [[Hinds (band)|Hinds]]. The song is from the band's 2024 album, ''[[Viva Hinds]]''. Later in July that year Beck also featured on the [[Orville Peck]] song "Death Valley High" off the latter's album ''[[Stampede (Orville Peck album)|Stampede]]''. A music video for the song was also filmed and feature appearances from the two musicians as well as drag queen [[Gigi Goode]] and actress [[Sharon Stone]].

==Musical style ==
Beck's musical style has been considered [[Alternative rock|alternative]]<ref>{{cite news|access-date=May 6, 2008|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1429687/19970227/beck.jhtml|title=Beck, Braxton, Babyface Share Grammy Wealth|publisher=MTV|date=February 27, 1997|archive-date=February 14, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080214224439/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1429687/19970227/beck.jhtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> and [[independent music|indie]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Old school night for 'The O.C.'|work=Los Angeles Times|date=February 27, 2005|page=E47|author= Hochman, Steve}}</ref> He has played many of the instruments in his music himself.<ref name="the information">{{cite news |access-date=May 6, 2008|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/reviews/album/11852928/review/11925431/the_information|title=The Information review |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080422063243/http://www.rollingstone.com/reviews/album/11852928/review/11925431/the_information |archive-date = April 22, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> Beck has also done some remixes for fellow artists, notably [[David Bowie]] and [[Björk]]. He has been known to synthesize several musical elements together in his music, including [[folk music|folk]], [[psychedelia]], [[electronic music|electronic]], [[country music|country]], [[Latin American music|Latin music]], [[hip hop music|hip hop]], [[funk]], [[soul music|soul]], [[blues]], [[noise music]], [[jazz]], [[art pop]] and many types of rock.<ref name="guero">{{cite magazine|access-date=May 6, 2008|url=https://nymag.com/nymetro/arts/music/pop/reviews/11605/|title=White-Boy Shuffle|magazine=[[New York (magazine)|New York]]|date=March 28, 2005|author=Beato, Greg|archive-date=June 26, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080626083246/http://nymag.com/nymetro/arts/music/pop/reviews/11605/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/02/28/arts/music-they-re-recording-but-are-they-artists.html|title=MUSIC; They're Recording, but Are They Artists?|first=Stephen|last=Holden|date=February 28, 1999|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=October 17, 2019|archive-date=November 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161130144527/http://www.nytimes.com/1999/02/28/arts/music-they-re-recording-but-are-they-artists.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Because of this unconventional approach, Beck has been described as a [[postmodernism|postmodern]] musician.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.npr.org/2017/10/20/558768104/colors-continues-beck-s-postmodern-pastiche |title='Colors' continues Beck's postmodern pastiche |last=Moon |first=Tom |date=October 20, 2017 |publisher=NPR |access-date=September 24, 2022}}</ref> He has also taken music from Los Angeles as a reference point in his songs.<ref name="guero" />

Pitchfork Media applauded ''Midnite Vultures'', saying, "Beck wonderfully blends [[Prince (musician)|Prince]], [[Talking Heads]], ''[[Paul's Boutique]]'', '[[Shake Your Bon-Bon]]', and Mathlete on ''Midnite Vultures'', his most consistent and playful album yet." The review commented that his mix of "goofy piety and ambiguous intent" helped the album.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=May 6, 2008|url=http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/record_review/15360-midnite-vultures?artist_title=15360-midnite-vultures|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080406103110/http://www.pitchforkmedia.com/article/record_review/15360-midnite-vultures?artist_title=15360-midnite-vultures|archive-date=April 6, 2008|title=Midnite Vultures review |publisher=[[Pitchfork Media]] }}</ref> A Beck song called "Harry Partch", a tribute to [[Harry Partch|the composer of the same name]] and his "corporeal" music, employs [[Harry Partch's 43-tone scale|Partch's 43-tone scale]].<ref>Beck.com [http://www.americansongwriter.com/2009/11/beck-salutes-harry-partch/ Beck salutes Harry Partch] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100121164753/http://www.americansongwriter.com/2009/11/beck-salutes-harry-partch/ |date=January 21, 2010 }}</ref>

==Art career==
During 1998, Beck's art collaborations with his grandfather Al Hansen were featured in an exhibition titled "Beck & Al Hansen: Playing With Matches", which showcased solo and collaborative [[collage]], assemblage, drawing and poetry works.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=April 25, 2008 |url=http://stewoo.net/beck/gallery/hansen_art/ |title=Playing with Matches |publisher=Stewoo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080509062301/http://stewoo.net/beck/gallery/hansen_art/ |archive-date=May 9, 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The show toured from the [[Santa Monica Museum of Art]] to galleries in New York City and [[Winnipeg]], Manitoba. Beck chose Winnipeg due to a family connection, as his grandfather gave their family stability through his work as a street car conductor in Winnipeg.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://nowtoronto.com/music/features/beck-interview-colors-winnipeg-u2-childish-gambino | title=Q&A: Why Beck nearly quit making albums | date=October 12, 2017 | access-date=September 26, 2022 | archive-date=September 26, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220926191914/https://nowtoronto.com/music/features/beck-interview-colors-winnipeg-u2-childish-gambino | url-status=dead }}</ref> A catalog of the show was published by Plug in Editions/Smart Art Press.<ref>{{cite news|access-date=April 25, 2008 |url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/latimes/access/29151145.html?dids=29151145:29151145&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT |title=ART; Beck's First Sampling; The pop star learned about collage from his larger-than life grandfather, Al Hansen. A Santa Monica show connects their careers. |work=Los Angeles Times |date=May 3, 1998 |author=McKenna, Kristine |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090504002839/https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/latimes/access/29151145.html?dids=29151145%3A29151145&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS%3AFT |archive-date=May 4, 2009 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Beck's nine-year relationship with designer Leigh Limon and their breakup is said to have inspired his 2002 album ''Sea Change''.<ref name="Salon">{{cite news | title = Guess I'm Doing Fine | date = October 2, 2002 | url = http://dir.salon.com/story/ent/music/feature/2002/10/02/beck/ | work = [[Salon.com]] | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071227182806/http://dir.salon.com/story/ent/music/feature/2002/10/02/beck/ | archive-date = December 27, 2007 | df = mdy-all }}</ref> He wrote most of the songs for the album one week after the breakup.<ref name="Time">{{cite news | title = Beck Gets (Kind of) Blue | date = September 22, 2002 | url = http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,1101020930-353545,00.html | magazine = [[Time (magazine)|Time]] | access-date = December 3, 2007 | archive-date = October 27, 2011 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20111027013610/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,1101020930-353545,00.html | url-status = dead }}</ref> In April 2004, Beck married actress [[Marissa Ribisi]], the twin sister of actor [[Giovanni Ribisi]], shortly before the birth of their son.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=April 26, 2008 |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P1-93658028.html |title=Beck Marries Marissa Ribisi |publisher=United Press International |date=April 20, 2004 }}{{dead link|date=February 2019|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref name="Spin">{{cite magazine | title = Beck Expecting Baby No. 2? | magazine = Spin | date = October 18, 2006 | url = https://www.spin.com/2006/10/beck-expecting-baby-no-2/ | access-date = July 13, 2008 | archive-date = May 31, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150531012020/http://www.spin.com/2006/10/beck-expecting-baby-no-2/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Their daughter was born in 2007.<ref name=nyt08/> Beck filed for divorce from Ribisi on February 15, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Singer Beck Files for Divorce From Wife of 14 Years |url=https://theblast.com/beck-divorce/ |website=The Blast |date=February 15, 2019 |access-date=February 16, 2019 |archive-date=February 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190216153246/https://theblast.com/beck-divorce/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Their divorce was finalized on September 3, 2021.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Beck Finalizes Divorce from Wife Marissa Ribisi as Couple Divvies Up Possessions — Including Banksys|url=https://people.com/music/beck-finalizes-divorce-from-wife-marissa-ribisi-as-couple-divvies-up-possessions/|date=September 8, 2021|access-date=October 2, 2021|magazine=People|quote=The musician's divorce from wife Marissa Ribisi was finalized on Sept. 3, more than two years after he first filed for divorce in February 2019 after nearly 15 years of marriage}}</ref>

Beck has described himself as both [[Jews|Jewish]]<ref name="Spin 2008-09" /> and a [[Scientologist]], but no longer identifies as the latter.<ref name="Sunday Tribune">{{cite web|last1=Dunphy|first1=Neil|title=A sort of homecoming|website=tribune.ie|url=http://www.tribune.ie/article/2005/jun/12/a-sort-of-homecoming/|publisher=Sunday Tribune|access-date=September 29, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100915054237/http://www.tribune.ie/article/2005/jun/12/a-sort-of-homecoming/|archive-date=September 15, 2010|date=June 12, 2005|quote='Yeah, I'm a Scientologist,' Beck resumes…}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> Through his parents, he has been involved in Scientology for most of his life; his ex-wife, Marissa, is also a second-generation Scientologist.<ref name="Celebrific">{{cite news|title=Scientologists Beck & Marissa Ribisi had their second child, daughter Tuesday in June 2007 |url=http://www.celebrific.com/scientologists-beck-marissa-ribisi-expecting-second-child/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071121053102/http://www.celebrific.com/scientologists-beck-marissa-ribisi-expecting-second-child/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 21, 2007 |publisher=Celebrific }}</ref> He publicly acknowledged his affiliation for the first time in a ''[[The New York Times Magazine|New York Times Magazine]]'' interview on March 6, 2005.<ref name=nyt05/><ref name = :"ny"/> Beck disavowed previous reports of his being a Scientologist in a November 2019 interview with the ''[[Sydney Morning Herald]]'' and said, "I think there's a misconception that I'm a Scientologist. I'm not a Scientologist. I don't have any connection or affiliation with it."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/culture/music/workaholic-beck-i-feel-a-little-guilty-if-something-s-too-easy-20191118-p53bnh.html|title='I think there's a misconception': musician Beck on Scientology|date=November 22, 2019|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191122225700/https://www.smh.com.au/culture/music/workaholic-beck-i-feel-a-little-guilty-if-something-s-too-easy-20191118-p53bnh.html|archive-date=November 22, 2019|access-date=November 22, 2019}}</ref> He added that "I was raised celebrating Jewish holidays, and I consider myself Jewish."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/celebrities/2019/11/22/beck-says-misconception-him-and-scientology/4277334002/|title=Beck says he's not a Scientologist after all: 'I think there's a misconception'|first=Charles|last=Trepany|website=Usatoday.com|access-date=September 17, 2020|archive-date=November 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191127215909/https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/celebrities/2019/11/22/beck-says-misconception-him-and-scientology/4277334002/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Beck's mother is artist/writer/performer [[Bibbe Hansen]], a former [[Andy Warhol]] [[The Factory]] collaborator.<ref name="Bibbe Hansen, bio">{{Cite web|url=https://bibbe.com/wp/bio/|title=Bio – Welcome|website=Bibbe.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://warholstars.org/superstars.html|title=Andy Warhol Superstars|website=Warholstars.org}}</ref> His siblings are [[fiber artist]] Channing Hansen (born in 1972 in Los Angeles)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stephenfriedman.com/artists/40-channing-hansen/|title=Channing Hansen|website=Stephenfriedman.com}}</ref> and poet Rain Whittaker.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://rogovoyreport.com/2016/02/16/lydia-lunch-bibbe-hansen-spotty-dog/ |title="Lydia Lunch and Bibbe Hansen (aka Beck's Mom) to Read at Spotty Dog" |magazine=The Rogovoy Report |date=February 16, 2016 }}</ref><ref name="Bibbe Hansen, bio"/>

Beck sustained a spinal injury while filming the music video for 2005's "[[E-Pro]]". The incident was severe enough to curtail his touring schedule for a few years, but he has since recovered.<ref name="Future Heart"/><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/beck-details-spinal-injury-that-nearly-ended-his-touring-career-20140314 |title=Beck Details Spinal Injury That Nearly Ended His Touring Career |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=March 14, 2014 |access-date=August 24, 2017 |archive-date=August 13, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813114315/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/beck-details-spinal-injury-that-nearly-ended-his-touring-career-20140314 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Beck primarily lived in [[Los Feliz, Los Angeles]] until 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.latimes.com/business/real-estate/story/2022-08-31/beck-asks-2-95-million-for-musician-friendly-home-in-los-feliz | title=Beck asks $2.95 million for musician-friendly home in los Feliz | website=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=August 31, 2022 }}</ref> He owns properties in California, Tennessee, and Arkansas.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sfgate.com/realestate/article/now-that-s-where-it-s-at-rent-beck-s-arkansas-18308465.php |title=Now That's 'Where It's At': Rent Beck's Arkansas Ranch House for Just $1,250 a Month |work=SF Gate |last=Natalie |first=Britney |date=August 25, 2023 |access-date=July 31, 2025}}</ref>

==Appearances in media==
The 1986 punk rock musical film ''[[Population: 1]]'', starred [[Tomata du Plenty]] of [[The Screamers]] and featured a young Beck in a small non-speaking role.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.population1movie.com/ |title=AgitPop and Cult Epics present Population: 1 |publisher=Population1movie.com |access-date=September 1, 2009 |archive-date=January 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190114044451/https://population1movie.com/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Beck also appears in ''[[Southlander]]'' (2001), an American independent film by Steve Hanft and Ross Harris.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Gordon|first1=Jeremy|title=Beck, Elliott Smith-Starring Cult Classic ''Southlander'' Gets Reissue|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/65382-beck-elliott-smith-starring-cult-classic-southlander-gets-reissue/|website=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]|access-date=October 16, 2017|date=May 10, 2016|archive-date=October 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016225946/https://pitchfork.com/news/65382-beck-elliott-smith-starring-cult-classic-southlander-gets-reissue/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Beck has performed on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' seven times. During his 2006 performance in the [[Hugh Laurie]] episode, Beck was accompanied by the puppets that had been used onstage during his world tour. He has made two cameo appearances as himself on ''Saturday Night Live'': one in a sketch about medicinal marijuana, and one in a VH1 ''[[Behind the Music]]'' parody that featured "Fat Albert & the Junkyard Gang".<ref>{{cite news|access-date=April 26, 2008 |url=http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-31512469_ITM |title=Bright spots scarce on 'SNL'. |work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=October 30, 2006|author=Ryan, Maureen |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080707122033/http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-31512469_ITM |archive-date = July 7, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> Beck performed a guest voice as himself on [[Matt Groening]]'s animated show ''[[Futurama]]'', in the episode "[[Bendin' in the Wind]]".<ref>{{cite web|access-date=April 26, 2008|url=http://www.scifi.com/sfw/screen/sfw10977.html|title=Futurama Volume Three DVD |publisher=[[Syfy|Sci Fi]]|date=May 3, 2004 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080701045811/http://www.scifi.com/sfw/screen/sfw10977.html |archive-date = July 1, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> He performed in episode 10 of the fourth season of ''[[The Larry Sanders Show]]'', in which the producer character [[List of characters on The Larry Sanders Show#Artie|Artie]] ([[Rip Torn]]) referred to him as a "[[hillbilly]] from outer space".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lastbroadcast.co.uk/music/v/5968-beck-gamma-ray.html |title=Beck: 'Gamma Ray' |publisher=LastBroadcast.co.uk |date=August 11, 2008 |access-date=September 1, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090504015618/http://www.lastbroadcast.co.uk/music/v/5968-beck-gamma-ray.html |archive-date=May 4, 2009 |url-status=usurped }}</ref> He also made a very brief voice appearance in the 1998 cartoon feature film ''[[The Rugrats Movie]]'',<ref>[[Internet Movie Database|IMDB]] entry for [https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0134067/fullcredits#cast ''The Rugrats Movie'' full cast & crew] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160927021807/http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0134067/fullcredits#cast |date=September 27, 2016 }}.</ref> and guest-starred as himself in a 1997 episode of ''[[Space Ghost Coast to Coast]]'' titled "Edelweiss".<ref>[[Internet Movie Database|IMDB]] entry for [https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0706050/ "Edelweiss"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170208001503/http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0706050/ |date=February 8, 2017 }}.</ref>

On January 22, 2010, Beck appeared on the last episode of ''[[The Tonight Show with Conan O'Brien]]'' as a backup guitarist for a [[Will Ferrell]]-led rendition of [[Lynyrd Skynyrd]]'s "[[Free Bird]]" alongside [[ZZ Top]] guitarist [[Billy Gibbons]], [[Ben Harper]], and O'Brien himself on guitar.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/tv/2010/01/22/2010-01-22_will_ferrell_and_wife_viveca_paulin_perform_freebird_with_conan_obrien_on_last_t.html |title=Will Ferrell and wife Viveca Paulin perform 'Free Bird' with Conan O'Brien on last 'Tonight Show' |newspaper=[[New York Daily News]] |date=January 23, 2010 |access-date=November 21, 2010 |location=New York |first=Soraya |last=Roberts |archive-date=January 26, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100126072711/http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/tv/2010/01/22/2010-01-22_will_ferrell_and_wife_viveca_paulin_perform_freebird_with_conan_obrien_on_last_t.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2010/01/23/will-ferrell-free-bird-vi_n_433975.html |title=Will Ferrell Sings Free Bird on Conan's Last Show (VIDEO) |work=[[The Huffington Post]] |date=January 23, 2010 |access-date=May 6, 2013 |location=New York |first=Alex |last=Leo |archive-date=June 22, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160622050641/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2010/01/23/will-ferrell-free-bird-vi_n_433975.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On March 1, 2014, Beck was the musical guest on a ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' episode hosted by [[Jim Parsons]]. Beck also appeared as himself in the 2017 film ''[[The Circle (2017 film)|The Circle]]'', giving a musical performance of the song "Dreams".

'''Mumford & Sons''' are an English [[folk rock]] band formed in [[London]] in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/london/content/articles/2008/10/29/londoncalling_mumford_and_sons_feature.shtml|title=Mumford and Sons|website=Bbc.co.uk}}</ref> The band consists of [[Marcus Mumford]] (lead vocals, guitar, drums), [[Ted Dwane]] (vocals, bass), and [[Ben Lovett (British musician)|Ben Lovett]] (vocals, keyboards).

Mumford & Sons have released five studio albums: ''[[Sigh No More (Mumford & Sons album)|Sigh No More]]'' (2009), ''[[Babel (Mumford & Sons album)|Babel]]'' (2012), ''[[Wilder Mind]]'' (2015), ''[[Delta (Mumford & Sons album)|Delta]]'' (2018), and ''[[Rushmere (album)|Rushmere]]'' (2025). Their debut ''Sigh No More'' peaked at number two on the [[UK Albums Chart]] and the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] in the US, with ''Babel'', ''Wilder Mind'' and ''Delta'' all debuting at number one in the US, the former becoming the fastest-selling rock album of the decade and leading to a headline performance at [[Glastonbury Festival in 2013]].<ref name=BabelUK/><ref name=BabelUS/>

The band has won music awards throughout their career, with ''Sigh No More'' earning the band the [[Brit Awards|Brit Award]] for [[2011 BRIT Awards|Best British Album]] in 2011, a [[Mercury Prize]] nomination and six overall [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Award]] nominations. The live performance at the 2011 Grammy ceremony with [[Bob Dylan]] and [[The Avett Brothers]] led to a surge in popularity for the band in the US. The band received eight total Grammy nominations for ''Babel'' and won the Grammy Award for [[Grammy Award for Album of the Year|Album of the Year]]. The band also won the Brit Award for [[2013 BRIT Awards|Best British Group]] in 2013 and an [[Ivor Novello Award]] for International Achievement in 2014.

==History==
===Early years (2007–2009)===
Mumford & Sons was formed in late 2007<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Mumford-and-Sons|title=Mumford & Sons &#124; British music group|website=Britannica.com|date=10 May 2023 }}</ref> by multi-instrumentalists [[Marcus Mumford]], [[Ted Dwane]], [[Ben Lovett (British musician)|Ben Lovett]], and [[Winston Marshall]]. Band members play acoustic guitar, drums, keyboard instruments, bass guitar, and traditional folk instruments such as [[banjo]], [[mandolin]] and [[resonator guitar]].<ref>{{Cite magazine <!-- Deny Citation Bot--> |magazine=Billboard|last=Kamps|first= Garrett|volume=127|issue=13|date=May 9, 2015|page=47 |id = {{ProQuest|1686669917}}|title=Bye, Banjos: Mumford & Sons Plug In and Rock Out}}</ref><ref name="bbc">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/london/content/articles/2008/10/29/londoncalling_mumford_and_sons_feature.shtml|title=London – Radio – Mumford and Sons|publisher=Bbc.co.uk|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> The band name originates from Marcus Mumford being the most visible member, organising the band and their performances. Lovett indicated that the name was meant to evoke the sense of an "antiquated family business name".<ref name=Collis>Collis, Clark (4 March 2011). [http://music-mix.ew.com/2011/03/04/mumford-and-sons-sigh-no-more/ "Mumford and Sons: Ben Lovett talks about playing with Dylan, recording with Ray Davies, and high-fiving R. Kelly"]. ''Entertainment Weekly Music Mix''. Retrieved 6 January 2011.</ref>

A handful of similar bands were increasing their visibility in [[West London (sub region)|West London]] around the same time, giving rise to the label "West London folk scene". Mumford downplays that characterisation as an exaggeration—Mumford & Sons and a few other folk acts just happened to be operating in the same general area at the time. In an interview with the ''[[Herald Sun]]'', Marcus Mumford said, "It's not folk really. Well, some of it is, and it's certainly not a scene. Someone got over-excited about a few bands who live in a hundred-mile radius and put it in a box to sell it as a package. It's a community, not a scene. It's not exclusive." Having developed in the same musical and cultural environment, Mumford & Sons' sound has been compared to that of artists such as [[Noah and the Whale]], [[Johnny Flynn (musician)|Johnny Flynn]] or [[Laura Marling]], whose backing band had included Marshall, Mumford, and Dwane.<ref>Walker, Tim (28 July 2008). [https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/reviews/mumford--sons-the-luminaire-london-878562.html "Mumford & Sons, The Luminaire, London"]. ''The Independent''. Retrieved 29 December 2010.</ref><ref name=ffs>{{cite web|url=http://www.forfolkssake.com/interviews/1375/for-folks-sake-interview-mumford-and-sons |title=From the archives: FFS interviews Mumford and Sons |last=Roberts |first=Lynn |work=For Folk's Sake |date=12 March 2011 |access-date=10 May 2015}}</ref>

In early 2008, the band began working with manager Adam Tudhope, who, as part of management company Everybody's, also represents [[Keane (band)|Keane]] and Laura Marling.<ref name="hitquarters.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.hitquarters.com/index.php3?page=intrview/opar/intrview_Bloom.html |title=Interview With Louis Bloom |publisher=[[HitQuarters]] |date=4 April 2011 |access-date=18 April 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110704123311/http://www.hitquarters.com/index.php3?page=intrview%2Fopar%2Fintrview_Bloom.html |archive-date=4 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It was through Tudhope's connection that Mumford & Sons was exposed to their future [[Artists and repertoire|A&R]] at Island, Louis Bloom, who began monitoring the band. Bloom told [[HitQuarters]] that they were still at a fledgling state and not yet ready for a label deal: "There was no one there for it, just a few friends, and they needed time to develop. Over the next six months I kept going to see them and they were literally picking up fans every time."<ref name="hitquarters.com"/>

In February 2008, the band completed an extensive UK tour with support from [[Alessi's Ark]], [[Sons of Noel and Adrian]], [[Peggy Sue (band)|Peggy Sue]] and others. June 2008 marked the band's first appearance at the [[Glastonbury Festival 2008|Glastonbury Festival]].<ref name="bbc"/> They also toured Australia with Laura Marling, whose disinclination to interact with audiences encouraged Mumford into the spotlight. The experience helped inform his attitude towards Mumford & Sons audiences, which is to interact frequently and to try to create a comfortable, casual atmosphere.<ref name=Betts>Betts, Marianne (25 March 2010). [http://www.heraldsun.com.au/entertainment/music/mumford-sons-have-taken-australia-by-storm/story-e6frf9hf-1225845393954 "Mumford & Sons have taken Australia by storm"]. ''Herald Sun''. Retrieved 24 January 2011.</ref> Mumford & Sons' first project was an EP entitled ''Love Your Ground'' which took a year to complete and was released in November 2008 on Chess Club Records.<ref name="bbc"/>

===''Sigh No More'' (2009–2012)===
Throughout 2008 and into 2009, Mumford & Sons performed in small to moderate venues in the UK and US, exposing audiences to ''Love Your Ground'' tracks and other material that would eventually become ''[[Sigh No More (Mumford & Sons album)|Sigh No More]]''. The band finally recorded ''Sigh No More'' with [[Markus Dravs]], who had produced albums with artists such as [[Arcade Fire]].<ref name=Betts /> At the time, band members did not even own their own instruments—Dravs initially turned them away when they showed up at the recording sessions empty-handed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/mumfordandsons/46631|title=Mumford And Sons: 'We were banished from studio by producer'|date=12 August 2009|work=NME|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> The only track from ''Love Your Ground'' to be included on ''Sigh No More'' was "[[Little Lion Man]]". The band told the ''Herald Sun'' that they self-financed the album to avoid the artistic and technical compromises that sometimes befall studio-financed projects.<ref name=Betts /> They toured again in support of Laura Marling in 2009, and Mumford & Sons was contributing musicians to her 2010 album ''[[I Speak Because I Can]]''.<ref name=Betts /><ref name="bbcsound">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/7766446.stm|title=BBC Sound of 2009: Mumford & Sons|publisher=News.bbc.co.uk|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref>
[[File:Mumfordandsons bristol.jpg|thumb|left|Mumford & Sons performing at Dot to Dot Festival in [[Bristol]] on 23 May 2009]]
In August 2009, Mumford & Sons signed a licensing deal to [[Island Records]] in the UK, to [[Dew Process]] in Australia and New Zealand, to [[Glassnote Records]] in North America and [[V2 Records|Cooperative Music]] in the rest of the world, and through its own label Gentlemen of the Road. Dew Process boss [[Paul Piticco]] signed the band after witnessing a US performance in 2009 and appreciating their "honest" approach and unique sound.<ref name=Betts /> Their debut album was released on 5 October 2009 with "Little Lion Man" as the lead single.

[[Dave Berry (presenter)|Dave Berry]] of [[XFM]] named "Little Lion Man" his record of the week, and in another interview with the band, Berry said "Screw 'of the week', it's my favourite track of the year." [[BBC Radio 1]] DJ [[Zane Lowe]] made "Little Lion Man" his "Reaction Record" on 27 July 2009,<ref name="Zane 2707">{{cite web|last=Lowe|first=Zane|date=27 July 2009|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/radio1/zanelowe/tracklistingarchive.shtml?20090727|title=Tracklisting – Monday 27 July 2009|publisher=[[BBC Radio 1]]|access-date=8 July 2011}}</ref> before naming it the "Hottest Record in the World" the following evening.<ref name="Zane 2807">{{cite web|last=Lowe|first=Zane|date=28 July 2009|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/radio1/zanelowe/tracklistingarchive.shtml?20090728|title=Tracklisting – Tuesday 28 July 2009|publisher=[[BBC Radio 1]]|access-date=8 July 2011}}</ref>

In their first performance on US network television, the band played "Little Lion Man" on CBS's ''[[Late Show with David Letterman]]'' on 17 February 2010. This appearance was followed by a performance of "[[The Cave (song)|The Cave]]" on ''[[The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson]]'' on 26 February 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/blog/index.php?blog=121&p=8004&more=1&c=1|title=Mumford And Sons censor 'Little Lion Man' for David Letterman|work=NME.COM|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> Mumford & Sons have been commercially successful in Australia and New Zealand. By January 2010, "Little Lion Man" topped the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2009|Triple J Hottest 100]] list for all of 2009, with its margin of victory the largest in the history of the chart.<ref>Gregg, Natalie (27 January 2010). [http://www.couriermail.com.au/entertainment/confidential/aussies-rock-in-triple-js-hottest-100/story-e6freq7o-1225823737803 "Aussies rock in Triple J's Hottest 100"]. ''The Courier-Mail''. Retrieved 21 February 2011.</ref> In November 2010, the band won an ARIA Music Award for Most Popular International Artist.<ref>Collett-White, Mike (20 November 2010). "Mumford & Sons top ARIA Awards". ''Billboard'' '''122''' (46): p. 32.</ref> ''Sigh No More'' first reached number 9 on the New Zealand charts in October 2010, and subsequently topped the chart in January 2011 due to the popularity of the singles from the album.<ref>"International Charts: Mumford & Sons' Sigh No More rallies around globe". ''Music Week'': p. 28 (22 January 2011).</ref>

In a March 2010 interview, [[Ray Davies]] announced that Mumford & Sons would be appearing on his forthcoming collaborations album.<ref>Uricheck, Mark (15 March 2010). [http://themusiciansvoice.blogspot.com/2010/03/chat-with-ray-davies.html "THE MUSICIAN'S VOICE: A Chat With The Legendary Ray Davies"]. Themusiciansvoice.blogspot.com. Retrieved 24 January 2011.</ref> Marcus Mumford confirmed this in an interview the same month, stating, "I am more excited about that than I have been about anything before in my life".<ref name=Betts /> Mumford & Sons performed the track "Days/This Time Tomorrow" along with Davies on 12 February 2010 on ''[[Later... with Jools Holland]]'' on the BBC.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p00bm7zp|title=BBC – Later live... with Jools Holland: Ray Davies & Mumford and Sons – Days/This Time Tomorrow|publisher=BBC|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref>

[[File:Mumford & Sons performing at Brighton Dome in October 2010 6.JPG|thumb|Marcus Mumford and Winston Marshall on stage in Brighton, 4 October 2010]]
In December 2010, Mumford & Sons earned Grammy Award nominations for Best New Artist and Best Rock Song ("Little Lion Man"). While they did not go on to win an award, the band performed their single "The Cave" at the Grammy ceremony. The performance earned positive media attention and boosted visibility for ''Sigh No More''—US sales increased by 99% in the period following the ceremony in February 2011.<ref name=Gundersen>Gundersen, Edna (24 February 2011). [https://www.usatoday.com/life/music/awards/grammys/2011-02-24-grammyboosts24_ST_N.htm "A Grammy performance is good for business"]. ''USA Today''. Retrieved 6 March 2011.</ref><ref name=NME>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/mumford-and-sons/55309|title=Mumford & Sons reach UK and US million sales landmark|date=7 March 2011|work=NME|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> The album subsequently peaked at number two on the UK Albums Chart and the ''Billboard'' 200 in the US.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/473022/now-37-livens-up-billboard-200-at-no-1-mumford-climb-to-no-2|title='Now 37' Livens Up Billboard 200 at No.&nbsp;1, Mumford Climb to No.&nbsp;2|date=16 February 2011|magazine=Billboard|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref>

On 7 December 2010, in collaboration with [[Dharohar Project]] and [[Laura Marling]], Mumford & Sons released an EP album recorded in Delhi, India. The album was recorded in a makeshift studio with traditional Rajasthani musicians and features four collaborations, including multicultural mash-ups of Marling's "Devil's Spoke" and Mumford & Sons' "To Darkness." ''Sigh No More'' is [[Music recording sales certification|certified]] 4× Platinum in the UK,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bpi.co.uk/|title=British Certification database|publisher=Bpi.co.uk|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> and 2× Platinum in the US.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH|title=US Certifications database|website=Riaa.com|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref>

The band continued to grow in popularity in 2011, winning several major awards and headlining larger shows and festivals. In February 2011, they received a [[European Border Breakers Award]] for their international success.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ec.europa.eu/culture/our-programmes-and-actions/doc1098_en.htm|title=Winners of the 2011 European Border Breakers Awards|date=12 March 2012|publisher=Ec.europa.eu|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> They received a Brit Award for British Album of the Year with ''Sigh No More'' and performed "Timshel" at the ceremony.<ref name=Collis /> UK sales of the album subsequently increased by 266 per cent.<ref name=NME /> While touring the United States in early 2011, the band began writing songs for the follow-up album. Keyboardist Ben Lovett credited the creative atmosphere of Nashville, Tennessee with easing the songwriting process.<ref>Montgomery, James (17 February 2011). [https://web.archive.org/web/20110220003451/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1658237/mumford-and-sons-sigh-no-more.jhtml "Mumford & Sons write Sigh No More follow-up while touring US"]. MTV. Retrieved 7 March 2011.</ref> While performing in Kansas City, Missouri on 3 June, the first stop of their US tour, the band announced they had been recording a new album, initially set to be released in late 2011.{{citation needed|date=August 2021}}

In April 2011, the group joined [[Old Crow Medicine Show]] and [[Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros]] on the inaugural [[Railroad Revival Tour]], which was inspired by the [[Festival Express]] tour across Canada in 1970 that included [[Buddy Guy]], [[Janis Joplin]], [[The Grateful Dead]] and [[The Band]].<ref name=Garvanin>{{cite news|last=Garvanin|first=Sinead|title=Mumford's railroad revival: The band boarded the Big Easy Express for a US tour with a difference|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/6music/news/20120227_mumford.shtml|newspaper=BBC Radio: 6 Music News|date=27 February 2012}}</ref> Travelling exclusively in vintage rail cars, the three bands performed in six "unique outdoor locations" over the course of a week starting in [[Oakland, California]].<ref>[http://railroadrevivaltour.com/tour-info/] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110424105718/http://railroadrevivaltour.com/tour-info/|date=24 April 2011}}</ref> Ketch Secor of Old Crow told ''[[American Songwriter]]'' that "It's like we left all our baggage at home and just brought our instruments", often writing new songs while on the train.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Moss|first=Marissa|title=Mumford & Co. Chase The American Dream in Big Easy Express|url=http://www.americansongwriter.com/2012/04/mumford-co-chase-the-american-dream-in-big-easy-express/|access-date=5 June 2012|magazine=American Songwriter|date=27 April 2012}}</ref> "We were just on these old rattling rails. It was a railroad odyssey that would have made [[Woody Guthrie|Woody]] and [[Doc Watson|Doc]] tip their hats and blow their whistles,"<ref name=DePaulia>{{cite news|last=Hoffman|first=Hannah|title=Q & A with Ketch Secor of Old Crow Medicine Show|url=http://www.depauliaonline.com/arts-life/q-a-with-ketch-secor-of-old-crow-medicine-show-1.2934905?pagereq=1#.UIiOQcXA_IM|access-date=25 October 2012|newspaper=The DePaulia|date=23 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131012021655/http://www.depauliaonline.com/arts-life/q-a-with-ketch-secor-of-old-crow-medicine-show-1.2934905?pagereq=1#.UIiOQcXA_IM|archive-date=12 October 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> he says. They appear in the musical documentary ''[[Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros#Big Easy Express and second studio album (Here)|Big Easy Express]]'', directed by Emmett Malloy, being made of the trip which premiered March 2012 at the [[South by Southwest]] Film Conference and Festival (SXSW Film) in [[Austin, Texas]]<ref name="indiewire.com">"[https://www.indiewire.com/article/sxsw-film-announced-2012-features-lineup SXSW Film Announces 2012 Features Lineup; 'Big Easy Express' to Close Festival]" by Nigel M. Smith, IndieWire.com; 1 February 2012.</ref>—winning the Headliner Audience Award.<ref name="hollywoodreporter.com">Fernandez, Jay A. (19 March 2012). "[https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/risky-business/sxsw-2012-big-easy-express-headliner-audience-award-301659 SXSW 2012: 'Big Easy Express' Wins Headliner Audience Award: Emmett Malloy's film follows folk rock bands on the road]" ''The Hollywood Reporter''.</ref> The film went on to win "Best Long Form Video" at the 2013 Grammy Awards.<ref name="grammy.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.grammy.com/nominees |title=The Official Site of Music's Biggest Night |publisher=GRAMMY.com |access-date=5 May 2015}}</ref>

Mumford & Sons played at the [[Glastonbury Festival]] on Friday 24 June 2011, and then embarked on a North American tour on which they frequently performed songs from the upcoming album.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/music/festivals/glastonbury/2011/artists/mumfordandsons/#p00hslzl |title=Glastonbury Festival |publisher=BBC |access-date=25 September 2012}}</ref> They recorded two songs for [[Andrea Arnold]]'s adaptation of ''[[Wuthering Heights (2011 film)|Wuthering Heights]]'', one of which (entitled "Enemy") is featured during the closing credits.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/archives/2011/05/23/mumford_sons_record_two_new_songs_for_andrea_arnolds_wuthering_heights |title=Mumford & Sons Record New Song "Enemy" For Andrea Arnold's 'Wuthering Heights' |last=Jagernuth |first=Kevin |date=23 May 2011 |work=[[Indie Wire]] |access-date=23 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110527051637/http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/archives/2011/05/23/mumford_sons_record_two_new_songs_for_andrea_arnolds_wuthering_heights |archive-date=27 May 2011 }}</ref> In June 2012, Mumford & Sons contributed the song "Learn Me Right" with [[Birdy (musician)|Birdy]] to the [[Pixar]] film ''[[Brave (2012 film)|Brave]]''.<ref>{{cite news |author=Bryko |title=First Details on 'Brave' Soundtrack! (UPDATE) |newspaper=Upcoming Pixar |date=1 May 2012 |url=http://pixarplanet.com/blog/first-news-on-brave-soundtrack |access-date=5 May 2012}}</ref>

===''Babel'' (2012–2014)===
Mumford & Sons released their second studio album ''[[Babel (Mumford & Sons album)|Babel]]'' on 24 September 2012, with a track listing of 12 songs,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/music/music-news/9403248/Mumford-and-Sons-announce-details-of-new-album-Babel.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/music/music-news/9403248/Mumford-and-Sons-announce-details-of-new-album-Babel.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Mumford & Sons announce details of new album, 'Babel'|date=16 July 2012|work=Telegraph.co.uk|access-date=28 September 2014}}{{cbignore}}</ref> and a deluxe edition containing three exclusive songs.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/mumford-sons-babel-sept-25-release-350369 | title=Mumford & Sons' 'Babel' to be Released Sept. 25 | work=The Hollywood Reporter | access-date=24 September 2012 | date=17 July 2012}}</ref> The lead single "[[I Will Wait]]" premiered on Zane Lowe's BBC Radio 1 show on 7 August.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/newsbeat-19175412|title=Mumford & Sons track played for first time on Radio 1|newspaper=BBC News|date=8 August 2012|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=LISTEN: Mumford & Sons unveil new single 'I Will Wait' |date=8 August 2012 |work=Clixie |access-date=17 September 2012 |url=http://www.clixie.co.uk/listen-mumford-sons-unveil-new-single-i-will-wait |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130419213822/http://www.clixie.co.uk/listen-mumford-sons-unveil-new-single-i-will-wait |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 April 2013 }}</ref> On 29 August 2012, Mumford & Sons recorded their concert at [[Red Rocks Amphitheatre]] in Colorado.<ref name=RedRocks/> The Concert was later released on DVD, Vinyl and on iTunes as "Road to Red Rocks". The performance of "I Will Wait" from the concert was released ahead of the DVD on 9 September as the band's official video for the song.<ref name=RedRocks>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/videos/mumford-sons-match-grandeur-of-red-rocks-on-i-will-wait-20120910|title=Mumford & Sons Match Grandeur of Red Rocks on 'I Will Wait'|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=10 September 2012|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> On 22 September 2012, the band performed two songs from the new album, "I Will Wait" and "Below My Feet", on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref>{{cite magazine |first=Logan |last=Nicklaus |title=Mumford & Sons Save the Day on 'SNL' |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=23 September 2012 |url= https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/news/mumford-sons-save-the-day-on-snl-while-joseph-gordon-levitt-falls-flat-20120923 |access-date=24 September 2012}}</ref>

[[File:Mumford_%26_Sons_at_the_2013_Brit_Awards.jpg|thumb|Mumford & Sons performing at the [[2013 Brit Awards]] held at the [[The O2 Arena (London)|O2 Arena]] in London, 20 February 2013]]
''Babel'' debuted at number one on the [[UK Albums Chart]] and the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]].<ref name=BabelUK>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2012/oct/03/mumford-sons-babel-fastest-seller-2012?newsfeed=true|title=New Mumford & Sons album Babel is fastest seller of 2012 in UK and US|work=the Guardian|date=3 October 2012|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref><ref name=BabelUS>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/474818/mumford-sons-babel-scores-biggest-debut-of-year-bows-at-no-1-on-billboard-200|title=Mumford & Sons' 'Babel' Scores Biggest Debut of Year, Bows at No. 1 on Billboard 200 Chart|date=3 October 2012|magazine=Billboard|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> It became the fastest selling album of 2012 in the UK, selling over 158,000 copies in its first week, and was the biggest selling debut of any album in 2012 in the US, selling 600,000 in its first week,<ref name=BabelUK/><ref name=BabelUS/> and over a million worldwide. Babel was also nominated for a brit award and a grammy award and won the latter. In December 2012, Winston Marshall told [[NME]] that the band was rehearsing and writing for their next album.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nme.com/news/mumford-and-sons/67593 |title=Mumford & Sons: 'We're already working on new songs' 2012 |work=NME |access-date=6 December 2012}}</ref>

The first phase of a [[Mumford & Sons: World Tour|2013 world tour]] in support of ''Babel'' was released in November 2012.<ref>{{cite web |author=Studio Juice, Ltd |title=Mumford & Sons – Live |publisher=Mumfordandsons.com |url=http://www.mumfordandsons.com/live |access-date=14 November 2012}}</ref> Their Gentlemen of the Road tour continued through 2013. After performing two shows on 8 & 9 June 2013 at the [[Austin360 Amphitheater]] in [[Austin, Texas]], bassist Ted Dwane checked into a hospital the next day. Surgeons found a [[blood clot]] on the surface of his brain and performed surgery to remove it. Heeding medical advice to aid Dwane's recovery, the band cancelled the rest of its ''Summer Stampede Tour'', including performances at the [[2013 Bonnaroo Music Festival]] and returned to the UK.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mumfordandsons.com/news/bonaroo-us-tour-a-statement-from-the-band|title=BONNAROO & US TOUR – A STATEMENT FROM THE BAND|date=14 June 2013 |publisher=Mumfordandsons.com|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> Dwane's surgery was successful, and his recovery was such that the band was able to headline the 2013 [[Glastonbury Festival]] on 30 June, with the band receiving acclaim for their performance.<ref>{{cite news|title=Glastonbury 2013 – review: Mumford and Sons give a triumphant performance on last night|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/reviews/glastonbury-2013--review-mumford-and-sons-give-a-triumphant-performance-on-last-night-8680541.html|newspaper=The Independent|date=2 August 2015}}</ref>

After first including select stopover cities in their 2012 Tour, the band again selected five cities in Canada, the UK and US to host a two-day festival with shows on multiple stages as well as various other activities and performances. The first stopover of the 2013 Gentleman of the Road tour was in [[Lewes]], East Sussex, from 19 to 20 July. Next was [[Simcoe, Ontario]] from 23 to 24 August, followed by [[Troy, Ohio]] from 30 to 31 August. The band rounded out their tour with stopovers in Guthrie, Oklahoma on 6 and 7 September and finally St. Augustine, Florida on 13 and 14 September. The Vaccines, Edward Sharpe & the Magnetic Zeros, Vampire Weekend, Old Crow Medicine Show, Yacht Club DJs, Alabama Shakes and various other bands also performed at many of the stopovers throughout the tour.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gentlemenoftheroad.com/home/|title=Gentlemen of the Road Stopovers 2013 – Mumford & Sons|publisher=Gentlemenoftheorad.com|access-date=28 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728013007/http://www.gentlemenoftheroad.com/home/|archive-date=28 July 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

After the end of the Babel tour, Mumford and Sons took a five-month break before returning to the studio in February 2014 to start work on their third album.<ref name=redfish /><ref name="huffingtonpost.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/09/21/mumford-and-sons-taking-a-break_n_3968067.html|title=Mumford and Sons taking a break|date=21 September 2013|work=The Huffington Post|access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/09/23/arts/music/mumford-sons-taking-a-break.html?_r=0 | work=The New York Times | first=Adam W. | last=Kepler | title=Mumford & Sons Taking a Break | date=22 September 2013}}</ref><ref name="New album">{{cite web|url=http://mumsonfans.com/mumford-will-start-writing-for-new-album-2014/|title=Mumford will start writing for new album|author=Kat|work=MumsonFans.com|access-date=28 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140922113147/http://mumsonfans.com/mumford-will-start-writing-for-new-album-2014/|archive-date=22 September 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="MumsonFans.com">{{cite web|url=http://mumsonfans.com/ben-lovett-announces-engagement-work-new-album/|title=Ben Lovett Announces his Engagement and Work on New Album|author=Kat|work=MumsonFans.com|access-date=28 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140906003951/http://mumsonfans.com/ben-lovett-announces-engagement-work-new-album|archive-date=6 September 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Mumford & Sons made their live return at the 375 capacity [[Oslo (Hackney)|Oslo]] venue in Hackney, London on 10 March 2015 with an intimate show for family and friends. ===''Delta'' (2018–2020)===
On 20 September 2018, the band released a new single, "[[Guiding Light (Mumford & Sons song)|Guiding Light]]", introducing their new album titled ''[[Delta (Mumford & Sons album)|Delta]]'' on [[BBC Radio 1]]. The second single, "[[If I Say]]", was released on 25 October.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p03hj9mt|title=Mumford & Sons' Party Playlist, Katy B + Mumford & Sons, Radio 1's Future Sounds with Annie Mac - BBC Radio 1|website=BBC|access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-45551673|title=Mumford & Sons 'grapple with manhood' for the first time|last=Savage|first=Mark|date=20 September 2018|work=BBC News|access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Mumford & Sons|title=Guiding Light|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B07HFH9WXK|access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> ''Delta'' was released on 16 November 2018, with appearances from [[Maggie Rogers]], Yebba, and [[Gill Landry]]. The LP was produced by [[Paul Epworth]], and was recorded mainly at [[The Church Studios]] in London.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/inside-mumford-sons-wildly-experimental-fourth-album-delta-726932/|title=Inside Mumford & Sons' Wildly Experimental Fourth Album 'Delta'|first1=Mark|last1=Sutherland|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=20 September 2018}}</ref> On 14 October 2019 Mumford & Sons was announced as a headliner at Okeechobee Music & Arts Festival.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tampabay.com/arts-entertainment/music/2019/10/14/okeechobee-music-festival-lineup-mumford-and-sons-bassnectar-more/|title=Okeechobee Music Festival lineup: Mumford and Sons, Bassnectar, more|website=Tampa Bay Times}}</ref> On 23 October 2019, the band released "[[Blind Leading the Blind (Mumford & Sons song)|Blind Leading the Blind]]", a song that was recorded during the ''Delta'' sessions but was not completed in time for the album.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://liveforlivemusic.com/news/mumford-sons-blind-leading-the-blind-2019/|title=Mumford & Sons Release New Single, "Blind Leading the Blind" &#91;Listen&#93;|date=23 October 2019}}</ref>

To commemorate the end of the [[Delta Tour]], which was cut short by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the band released a six-track [[Album#Live|live EP]] titled ''Delta Tour EP'', which consisted of various live recordings from the tour. The release included live covers of "[[Hurt (Nine Inch Nails song)|Hurt]]" by [[Nine Inch Nails]],  "Blood" by [[The Middle East (band)|the Middle East]], and "[[With a Little Help from My Friends]]" by [[the Beatles]]. Featured guest artists included [[Gang of Youths]] and [[the Milk Carton Kids]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.jambase.com/article/mumford-sons-delta-tour-ep-live-compilation/amp|work=JamBase|title= Mumford & Sons Announce 'Delta Tour EP' Live Compilation|first=Nate|last=Todd|date=5 November 2020|access-date=4 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://open.spotify.com/album/4DNU3xDmnwdwNoep47QR22|title=Delta Tour EP (Live)|website=[[Spotify]] }}</ref> The band also released an early demo of the ''Delta'' track "Forever", subtitled "garage version", on 8 May 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thebluegrasssituation.com/read/watch-mumford-sons-forever-garage-version/|work=The Bluegrass Situation|title=Watch: Mumford & Sons, "Forever (Garage Version)"|date=11 May 2020|access-date=4 February 2024}}</ref>

===Marshall's departure and Mumford's solo album (2021–2022)===
In March 2021, Marshall praised [[Andy Ngo]] on Twitter for his 2021 book ''Unmasked'', which is deeply critical of the [[Antifa (United States)|antifa]] movement, saying "Congratulations @MrAndyNgo. Finally had the time to read your important book. You're a brave man". Marshall's tweet received backlash and criticism on social media.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/mumford-sons-winston-marshall-praises-brave-right-wing-agitator-andy-ngo-2895342|title=Mumford & Sons' Winston Marshall praises "brave" agitator Andy Ngo|last=Richards|first=Will|date=7 March 2021|work=NME|access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref> Following this, Marshall apologised and announced he was taking time away from the band.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/mumford-sons-winston-marshall-andy-ngo-1139278/|title=Mumford and Sons' Winston Marshall 'Taking Time Away From Band' After Praising Conservative Provocateur|date=10 March 2021 |magazine=Rolling Stone|last=Kreps|first=Daniel|access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref> On 24 June 2021, Marshall stated that his apology had been made to minimise the impact on the band at large. In his published statement he rejected being labelled as far-right for his recommendation of a book critical of the far-left, saying that to call him a fascist was "ludicrous beyond belief". He announced that he was leaving Mumford & Sons so that he could speak his mind on controversial issues without his bandmates and their families suffering the consequences.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Marshall|first=Winston|date=24 June 2021|title=Why I'm Leaving Mumford & Sons|url=https://mrwinstonmarshall.medium.com/|access-date=24 June 2021|website=Medium|language=en}}</ref>

On 16 September 2022, Mumford released his debut solo studio album, ''[[Self-Titled (Marcus Mumford album)|Self-Titled]]''. The record was preceded by three singles: "[[Cannibal (Marcus Mumford song)|Cannibal]]", "[[Grace (Marcus Mumford song)|Grace]]", and "Better Off High".<ref name=SelfTitledRS>{{Cite magazine|url= https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/marcus-mumford-self-titled-1234587637/|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|title=Marcus Mumford Deals With Isolation and Processes Anger on '(Self-Titled)'|first=Maura|last=Johnson|date=8 September 2022|access-date=4 February 2024}}</ref> In late November 2022, Mumford teased a new studio album from the band, stating that "the next thing really is to get in the room with the boys in the band and start playing each other the songs we've written."<ref name=NMErecord5>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/marcus-mumford-teases-new-mumford-sons-album-3355266|work=[[NME]]|title=Marcus Mumford teases new Mumford & Sons album|first=Will|last=Richards|date=24 November 2022|access-date=4 February 2024}}</ref>

The band debuted a new song, "Maybe", live on 26 August 2023 at Beach Road Weekend Festival.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ux4F-mgpf00|title=@MumfordandSons / Timshel & New Song / @beachroadweekend4998 / August 26, 2023|date=28 August 2023 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/mumford-and-sons/2023/veterans-memorial-park-vineyard-haven-ma-73a50269.html|title=Mumford & Sons Setlist at Beach Road Weekend 2023|website=Setlist.fm}}</ref> On 16 January 2024, the band released "Good People", a collaboration with [[Pharrell Williams]]. The single marks the band's first new music release since the departure of Marshall.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.gq.com/story/pharrells-louis-vuitton-collaboration-mumford-and-sons|work=[[GQ]]|title=The Story Behind Pharrell's Surprise New Louis Vuitton Collaboration With Mumford & Sons|first=Samuel|last=Hine|date=16 January 2024|access-date=16 January 2024}}</ref>

===''Rushmere'' (2025–present)===
On 15 January 2025, Mumford & Sons announced their first album in seven years, ''[[Rushmere (album)|Rushmere]]'', to be released 28 March. The announcement was made alongside an official trailer including snippets of new music and behind-the-scenes studio footage. Its lead single, also titled "Rushmere" was released 2 days later on 17 January. The band went on to confirm that the track and album were co-produced by [[Dave Cobb]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.nme.com/news/music/mumford-sons-announce-first-album-in-seven-years-RUSHMERE-3829463|title= Mumford & Sons announce first new album in seven years, ''RUSHMERE''|website= [[NME]]|date= 16 January 2025}}</ref>

The band relaunched the [[Railroad Revival Tour]] in the summer of 2025, playing venues along the [[East Coast of the United States]] alongside other folk musicians.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Blistein |first=Jon |date=2025-05-13 |title=Mumford & Sons Are Reviving Their Railroad Revival Tour |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/mumford-and-sons-2025-railroad-revival-tour-1235337852/ |access-date=2025-08-07 |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Musical style and development==
[[File:Mumford drums.jpg|thumb|right|The band members play multiple instruments in live performances. Here Marcus Mumford sits at a drum kit.]]
Mumford & Sons have been described by ''The Hollywood Reporter'' and ''[[Forbes]]'' as a [[folk rock]] band.<ref name="hollywoodreporter.com"/><ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www3.forbes.com/business/the-worlds-highest-paid-musicians-of-2016/4/ |title=The World's Highest-Paid Musicians Of 2016 |author=Greenburg, Zack O'Malley |magazine=[[Forbes]] |date=December 2016 |access-date=14 December 2016 |author-link=Zack O'Malley Greenburg |archive-date=16 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180716082441/https://www3.forbes.com/business/the-worlds-highest-paid-musicians-of-2016/4/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> They began by using [[bluegrass music|bluegrass]] and [[Folk music|folk]] instrumentation, with the core instruments of acoustic guitar, banjo, piano and a double bass, played with a rhythmic style based in [[alternative rock]] and folk. In the documentary ''Big Easy Express'', Marcus Mumford recognises the [[Old Crow Medicine Show]] influence: "I first heard Old Crow's music when I was, like, 16, 17, and that really got me into, like, folk music, bluegrass. I mean, I'd listened to a lot of Dylan, but I hadn't really ventured into the country world so much. So Old Crow was the band that made me fall in love with country music."<ref name=Hight>{{cite news|last=Hight|first=Jewly|title=Old Crow Medicine Show: The Wheel Of Life|url=http://www.americansongwriter.com/2012/08/old-crow-medicine-show-the-wheel-of-life/|access-date=5 September 2012|newspaper=American Songwriter|date=30 August 2012}}</ref> Mumford acknowledges that "the band inspired them to pick up the banjo and start their now famous country nights in London." Ketch Secor, Old Crow front-man, concurs: "Those boys took the message and ran with it."<ref name=Talbott>{{cite news|last=Talbott|first=Chris|title=Old Crow Medicine Show starts new chapter with 'Carry Me Back'|url=http://blogs.tennessean.com/tunein/2012/08/08/old-crow-medicine-show-starts-new-chapter-with-carry-me-back/|access-date=26 September 2012|newspaper=The Tennessean|date=8 August 2012}}</ref> {{blockquote|[[Emmylou Harris]] was "among the gateway artists who helped Mumford and bandmates Ben Lovett, Ted Dwane and Winston Marshall discover their love for American roots music. It started with the [[O Brother, Where Art Thou? (soundtrack)|'O Brother, Where Art Thou?' soundtrack]] ... That eventually led them to the Old Crow Medicine Show and then deep immersion in old-timey sounds from America's long-neglected past."<ref name=Talbott2>{{cite news|last=Talbott|first=Chris|title=Emmylou, Mumford & Sons team for 'CMT Crossroads'|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/huff-wires/20120926/us-music-mumford-and-emmylou/|access-date=26 September 2012|newspaper=Huffington Post|date=26 September 2012}}</ref>}}

Much of Mumford & Sons' lyrical content has a strong literary influence, their debut album name deriving from a line in [[William Shakespeare]]'s ''[[Much Ado About Nothing]]''. The track "Sigh No More" includes lines from the play such as ''Serve God love me and mend'', ''For man is a giddy thing'', and ''One foot in sea and one on shore.'' The title of the song "Roll Away Your Stone" is an allusion to ''[[Macbeth]]''; the song includes the line ''Stars hide your fires/ And these here are my desires'' which borrows and pares down Macbeth's line in act 1, scene 4: ''Stars, hide your fires,/ Let not light see my black and deep desires.''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://shakespeare-navigators.com/macbeth/T14.html|title=MACBETH, Act 1 Scene 4|publisher=Shakespeare-navigators.com|access-date=24 September 2012}}</ref> Additionally, "The Cave" includes several references to ''[[The Odyssey]]'', in particular the sirens that Odysseus encounters on his journey home. The song also contains many references to [[G. K. Chesterton]]'s book, ''St. Francis of Assisi'', in which Chesterton uses [[Allegory of the Cave|Plato's Cave]] as a way of explaining how [[Francis of Assisi|St. Francis]] views the world from God's perspective. Both "Timshel" and "Dust Bowl Dance" draw heavily from the [[John Steinbeck]] novels ''[[Of Mice and Men]]'', ''[[East of Eden (novel)|East of Eden]]'' and ''[[The Grapes of Wrath]]''.

The band's change in sound on their third album was described by Lovett as a "natural departure". At the end of the ''Babel'' tour Winston Marshall traded his banjo for electric guitar in sound checks and Mumford started playing more drums as the band jammed on heavy instrumentals and even some Radiohead tunes. Banjo, an instrument that had become synonymous with the band, does not feature on the record. ''[[NME]]''<ref name="nme.com"/> reported that the band's sound is "More expansive than ever and decidedly heavier, thanks to the shift in instrumentation." The group also employed a full drumkit instead of kick drum. "We've had our standard line-up of instruments for the last six years and we felt like that was our palette, [but] we started picking up other stuff," said Lovett. "It's a very natural departure from some of that rootsier stuff."<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Doyle |first=Patrick |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/mumford-sons-talk-going-electric-on-new-album-wilder-mind-20150302?page=2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150305064359/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/mumford-sons-talk-going-electric-on-new-album-wilder-mind-20150302?page=2 |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 March 2015 |title=Page 2 of Mumford & Sons Talk Going Electric on New Album 'Wilder Mind' |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=2 March 2015 |access-date=5 May 2015}}</ref>

Lovett told ''NME'' that working with [[James Ford (musician)|James Ford]] for ''Wilder Mind'' was part of trying something new. "We felt a need for change. Not from Markus [Dravs], but he was so closely attached to those first two records that as we had taken that time off, we wanted to try doing something new. It felt like, if we do our third record with Markus, does that mean we do our ninth and 10th records with Markus? At some point you have to try different things, as we collectively felt like it was time to try other stuff. Markus knows that we might well make the next record with him. We definitely haven't broken up [with Dravs], we're just playing the field!"<ref name="nme.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/mumford-and-sons/83246 |title=NME News Mumford & Sons say going electric on new album is 'a natural departure' |website=NME |date=3 March 2015 |access-date=5 May 2015}}</ref>

===Lyrical themes===
Many of Mumford & Sons' songs seem to be "laden with the themes and imagery of faith - often drawing specifically upon the [[Christian]] tradition."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sj-r.com/story/lifestyle/faith/2013/04/13/commentary-marcus-mumford-is-on/41725373007/ |title=Marcus Mumford is on a journey, just like you |newspaper=The State Journal-Register |publisher=The State Journal Register |date=13 April 2013 |access-date=6 March 2024}}</ref> Songs that have been emphasised as correlating with Christian elements include "[[Believe (Mumford & Sons song)|Believe]]", "[[Guiding Light (Mumford & Sons song)|Guiding Light]]" and "[[Roll Away Your Stone]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://relevantmagazine.com/culture/mumford-sons-10-best-songs-about-wrestling-faith/ |title=Mumford & Sons' 10 Best Songs About Wrestling with Faith |publisher=Relevant Magazine |date=28 September 2018 |access-date=6 March 2024}}</ref> The band's lead singer, Marcus Mumford, was also raised in a devout Christian home, with his parents, Eleanor and John Mumford leading the Vineyard Church in the United Kingdom and Ireland.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/2015/3/11/20560482/mumford-and-sons-latest-song-believe-stays-faithful-to-the-band-s-christian-roots/ |title=Mumford and Sons' latest song 'Believe' stays faithful to the band's Christian roots |publisher=Deseret News |date=11 March 2015 |access-date=6 March 2024}}</ref> However, when questioned about their Christian affiliation, Mumford was quick to push away from any form of religious adherence, stating, "I wouldn't call myself a Christian... I've kind of separated myself from the culture of Christianity... [but my] spiritual journey is a work in progress."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/mumford-sons-rattle-and-strum-78883/#ixzz3XWyfvpax |title=Mumford & Sons: Rattle and Strum |publisher=Rolling Stone |date=28 March 2013 |access-date=6 March 2024}}</ref> Later, Mumford reaffirmed this position on behalf of the band, responding to a question about whether the band's songs relate to Mumford's journey back to the Christian faith of his childhood by stating, "It's not about that all, sorry! I don't even call myself a Christian. Spirituality is the word we engage with more. We're fans of faith, not religion."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bigissue.com/culture/music/mumford-sons-fans-faith-not-religion/ |title=Mumford & Sons: "We're fans of faith, not religion" |publisher=the Big Issue |date=3 October 2012 |access-date=6 March 2024}}</ref>

==Other ventures==
In 2009, the band founded Gentlemen of the Road, a live promotions company, record label and organiser of the global series of Stopover Festivals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gentlemenoftheroad.com |title=Tickets, Line-up, News & Info |publisher=Gentlemenoftheroad.com |access-date=5 May 2015}}</ref> These festivals tend to take place in towns and villages not normally toured in by bands or singers in an effort to bring money to the place and help businesses there.{{failed verification|date=March 2017}} The band handpicks the supporting acts which play for the Stopover Festivals. These include bands such as [[Foo Fighters]], [[The Flaming Lips]], [[The Vaccines]], [[The Maccabees (band)|The Maccabees]] and [[Jenny Lewis]], amongst others.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mumfordandsons.com/news/gentlemen-of-the-road-stopovers-2015/ |title=Gentlemen Of The Road Stopovers 2015 - Mumford & Sons |publisher=Mumfordandsons.com |date=18 August 2016 |access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref>
